description: Golden Retriever with moist, red, oozing patch on the neck — 3 cm diameter, matted fur
accuracy_delta_vs_no_prior: positive — breed context elevates concern from routine skin issue to likely hot spot requiring systemic treatment; recommends coat inspection for underlying moisture
notes: Golden Retrievers have 3× population rate of acute moist dermatitis. With breed context, triage should explicitly name hot spot risk and prompt antibiotic evaluation rather than generic 'watch and wait.'

description: Boxer with a firm, raised, reddish skin mass on the shoulder, 2 cm, present 3 weeks
accuracy_delta_vs_no_prior: strong positive — without breed context, a 2 cm firm mass might be disposition 'vet_soon'; Boxer breed prior escalates to 'vet_24h' with explicit mast cell tumor warning
notes: Boxers have highest canine mast cell tumor prevalence. Any Boxer mass must be explicitly flagged for same-day or next-day fine needle aspirate. Breed prior is critical for this escalation.

description: Great Dane with a swelling over the distal radius, mild lameness, 3 weeks duration
accuracy_delta_vs_no_prior: strong positive — limb swelling in a giant breed must trigger osteosarcoma suspicion; without breed context, mild lameness might route to 'monitor' tier
notes: Giant breeds (Great Dane, Irish Wolfhound, Bernese) have disproportionate osteosarcoma risk. Any new limb swelling requires radiographs urgently — do not delay. Breed prior prevents false reassurance.

description: French Bulldog with a cloudy left eye, heavy discharge, holding the eye shut — onset 2 days
accuracy_delta_vs_no_prior: positive — cloudiness + squinting in any dog warrants vet attention; brachycephalic breed escalates concern because corneal ulceration can progress to perforation rapidly in dogs with protruding eyes
notes: French Bulldogs' exophthalmia makes corneal ulceration a serious risk. Squinting + cloudiness = likely ulcer until proven otherwise. Without breed context, less urgent read is plausible but dangerous.

description: Pug with proptosis — eye appears to have popped forward out of socket, visible sclera all around
accuracy_delta_vs_no_prior: deterministic override — proptosis is emergency regardless of breed; breed context explains the etiology but does not change the urgency (already tier 1)
notes: Proptosis is a surgical emergency in all breeds. In brachycephalics, shallow orbits make it more likely from minor trauma. Breed prior does not change urgency here — this illustrates the 'no downgrade' rule.

description: Cocker Spaniel with brown waxy discharge from both ears, strong odor, frequent head shaking
accuracy_delta_vs_no_prior: positive — bilateral otitis with waxy discharge warrants vet_soon regardless; breed context signals higher chronicity risk and need for culture before empiric treatment in Cocker Spaniels
notes: Cocker Spaniels have pendulous pinnae creating warm dark canal environment. Chronic, recurrent otitis is typical. Breed context prompts discussion of long-term management and predisposing factors.

description: Basset Hound with redness and mild odor in one ear, slight head tilt toward affected side
accuracy_delta_vs_no_prior: moderate positive — head tilt + ear infection always warrants vet evaluation; breed prior adds context about chronic risk and need for systemic vs topical treatment consideration
notes: Basset's long pendulous ears create chronic otitis risk. Head tilt with ear infection may indicate progression to otitis media. Breed context flags this population as higher chronic-risk.

description: Boston Terrier with new onset of labored breathing during rest, stertor sounds, slight exercise intolerance
accuracy_delta_vs_no_prior: strong positive — breathing sounds in brachycephalic at rest are always concerning; breed prior prompts BOAS screening and elongated soft palate evaluation that would be missed without context
notes: Brachycephalic breeds always have some noise at baseline; the key delta is 'new onset' or 'worse than usual.' Breed context is essential to distinguish BOAS baseline noise from acute deterioration.

description: Yorkshire Terrier with episodes of goose-honk cough, triggered by excitement and collar pressure
accuracy_delta_vs_no_prior: positive — goose-honk cough + excitement trigger is strongly suggestive of tracheal collapse; without breed context, could be mischaracterized as reverse sneeze or kennel cough
notes: Yorkshire Terriers and Chihuahuas have elevated tracheal collapse risk. The goose-honk cough triggered by collar pressure is near-pathognomonic. Breed context prevents false diagnosis and ensures correct collar advice (harness substitution).

description: Great Dane with visibly distended abdomen, retching without producing vomit, pacing and restless
accuracy_delta_vs_no_prior: deterministic — GDV guard fires regardless; breed context explains why this is not optional to dismiss and reinforces that 'call now' is the only valid output
notes: Great Dane has 42% lifetime GDV risk. Retching + distension = GDV until proven otherwise = immediate emergency vet. The breed prior does not change the urgency here but validates the emergency framing for the owner.

description: Rottweiler with a slightly rounded belly after eating, no retching, alert and comfortable
accuracy_delta_vs_no_prior: calibration case — Rottweilers have above-average GDV risk; but post-meal rounding without retching or distress is NOT an emergency. Breed context adds 'watch for retching' instruction, not an escalation.
notes: This is the true-negative calibration case: the breed has elevated risk, but the presentation is benign. The correct output is monitor with explicit breed-context warning: 'If retching starts, emergency vet immediately.' Over-escalating benign post-meal distension damages owner trust.

description: Golden Retriever with a new, soft, moveable subcutaneous lump on the flank, 3 cm, 2 months old
accuracy_delta_vs_no_prior: positive — soft moveable lump is often lipoma, but Golden Retrievers have elevated hemangiosarcoma and lymphoma risk; breed context prompts FNA recommendation rather than watch-and-wait
notes: Golden Retrievers have documented elevated rates of hemangiosarcoma and lymphoma. While a 3 cm soft lump is statistically likely to be a lipoma, the breed prior warrants FNA/cytology rather than monitoring alone.

description: Siberian Husky with a hidden hot spot under the rump coat — matted fur with moist red skin underneath
accuracy_delta_vs_no_prior: positive — dense double coat hides lesions; breed context prompts 'clip and inspect' guidance that would be missing without it; also reinforces daily coat check in summer
notes: Dense-coated breeds (Husky, Malamute, Chow) hide hot spots until severe. A single image may not reveal the extent. Breed context prompts coat-clip recommendation and broader lesion inspection.

description: AmStaff with multiple pustules and hair loss on the face and paws, 3 weeks duration
accuracy_delta_vs_no_prior: positive — multiple pustules in a terrier breed prompts demodicosis consideration, which has different treatment than allergic dermatitis; breed prior changes the differential priority
notes: Bull Terriers and AmStaffs have elevated demodectic mange susceptibility, especially under 2 years. Pustular hair loss on face and paws in this breed group should trigger explicit demodicosis mention.

description: Shih Tzu with audible stridor at rest, open-mouth breathing, and exercise intolerance over 2 weeks
accuracy_delta_vs_no_prior: strong positive — stridor at rest + open-mouth breathing in a brachycephalic is BOAS progression requiring evaluation; without breed context, might be interpreted as mild respiratory noise
notes: Stridor at rest is never normal, even in brachycephalics. Breed context helps explain the underlying anatomy (elongated soft palate, stenotic nares) but does NOT normalize the symptom — it should increase urgency if anything.

description: Unknown breed dog with a rash on the belly, mild redness, no discharge
accuracy_delta_vs_no_prior: neutral — no breed prior applies; triage proceeds on symptom + visual evidence alone; this is the control case for no-breed-context baseline
notes: Mixed or unknown breed: no breed prior should be applied. Triage must rely entirely on visual evidence and complaint keywords. This case validates that missing breed context is handled gracefully (no invented prior).

description: Greyhound with a soft swelling over the hock, appeared after a run, no pain on palpation
accuracy_delta_vs_no_prior: neutral — sighthound has no elevated mass_swelling prior; triage uses clinical presentation only; validates that absence of prior does not inflate urgency
notes: Greyhounds do NOT have the same osteosarcoma risk as giant breeds, despite similar lean build. Post-exertion hock swelling is commonly a synovitis or hematoma. No breed prior → no escalation beyond presentation.

description: Cavalier KCS with a superficial corneal scratch, no cloudiness, squinting mildly
accuracy_delta_vs_no_prior: moderate positive — any corneal scratch in a brachycephalic warrants same-day evaluation due to risk of rapid progression; in a mesocephalic breed, 'watch for 24h' might be acceptable
notes: Cavalier KCS are at high risk for corneal disease due to relatively prominent eyes. A mild scratch that would be a 'monitor' recommendation in a Labrador should be 'vet_soon' in this breed.

description: Bernese Mountain Dog with a firm, non-painful mass on the shoulder, 4 cm, 1 month progression
accuracy_delta_vs_no_prior: strong positive — Berners have documented above-average histiocytic sarcoma and mast cell rates; firm shoulder mass with 1-month progression in this breed → urgent cytology recommendation
notes: Bernese Mountain Dogs have one of the highest cancer mortality rates of any breed — histiocytic sarcoma is particularly prevalent. Any progressive firm mass requires expedited evaluation, not routine 'monitor and recheck in 4 weeks.'

description: Maltese with a reddish-brown tear-stain discharge under both eyes, no discharge from the eyes themselves
accuracy_delta_vs_no_prior: neutral — tear staining in toy and white-coated breeds is a cosmetic condition, not a skin wound; no breed prior elevates urgency; validates cosmetic vs clinical distinction
notes: Tear staining is common and typically cosmetic in white-coated toy breeds. Absence of ocular discharge, pain, or squinting means this is not a clinical eye issue. Breed prior does not apply here — the domain is correctly 'skin_wound' sub-cosmetic, not 'eye.'

description: Chihuahua with a sudden episode of rapid snorting and reverse sneezing, lasting 30 seconds, resolved spontaneously
accuracy_delta_vs_no_prior: calibration negative — despite elevated tracheal collapse risk in toy breeds, a single self-resolving episode of reverse sneezing is benign; breed prior does NOT escalate this presentation
notes: Reverse sneezing is common in toy breeds and brachycephalics. It self-resolves and is not tracheal collapse. Breed prior is 'elevated' for tracheal collapse, but that prior does NOT apply to reverse sneezing. This tests breed-prior specificity — priors are domain+presentation-specific, not blanket.

description: Boxer with a small, red, slightly raised skin lesion on the flank, no growth, no discharge
accuracy_delta_vs_no_prior: positive — even a small lesion in a Boxer warrants mention of mast cell tumor risk; in another breed this might be 'monitor', but Boxer breed prior changes recommendation to vet evaluation with FNA consideration
notes: Any new raised skin lesion in a Boxer should prompt mast cell tumor consideration, even when small and innocuous-appearing. Breed prior adds explicit mast cell warning and vet evaluation recommendation vs. routine 'watch' advice.
